extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, auditors, and corporate compliance officers preparing SEC climate-related financial disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluation criteria for including climate-related expenditures, capitalized costs, charges, losses, and related contextual information in a registrant's audited financial statement notes, plus structured data tagging and related thresholds/attribution rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of expenditures, capitalized costs, charges, and losses from severe weather and natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require disclosure of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope narrowed relative to proposal to limit ambiguity. The disclosures are intended to help investors evaluate exposure to physical risks and differentiate company-specific (diversifiable) from non-diversifiable risks. Concerns about differing company interpretations are mitigated by subjecting disclosures to ICFR and independent audit and by requiring contextual information (inputs, assumptions, judgments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of expenditures and losses from carbon offsets and renewable energy credits (RECs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure of expenditures expensed, capitalized costs, and losses resulting from the purchase and use of carbon offsets and RECs if those were used as a material component of a registrant's plans to achieve disclosed climate-related targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose aggregate amounts expensed, aggregate capitalized amounts recognized, and aggregate losses on capitalized offsets/RECs. These are discrete and expected to be easily identifiable; incremental compliance and audit costs expected to be relatively small. Purpose: allow investors to understand approach to meeting targets and interactions with other regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual information accompanying financial statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must provide contextual information explaining the basis for the financial statement disclosures, including a description of any significant inputs and assumptions used, significant judgments made to calculate the disclosures, and other information important to an investor's understanding of the financial statement effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require use of financial information consistent with the scope of consolidated financial statements and the same accounting principles (GAAP). Contextual information and consistent presentation should improve comparability and decision-usefulness. Level of detail should be driven by facts and circumstances; flexibility is intended to balance relevance with cost. Some commenters were skeptical about value of contextual info; Commission retains flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective presentation / historical periods required
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules require presentation of the financial statement disclosures on a prospective basis only: disclosure for the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year and, to the extent previously disclosed or required, for historical fiscal year(s) included in the consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lowers initial compliance costs but delays availability of year-over-year comparisons for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of impacts on financial estimates and assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose whether the estimates and assumptions used to produce the consolidated financial statements were materially impacted by exposures to risks and uncertainties associated with, or known impacts from, severe weather events and other natural conditions or any disclosed climate-related targets or transition plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosures inform investors about the sensitivity of financial information to climate-related risks (e.g., how a net-zero target affected assumptions). Benefit depends on whether registrants would have disclosed such impacts absent the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in audited financial statement note and subject to ICFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Required disclosures must be included in a note to the financial statements and thus audited by an independent registered public accounting firm under existing Commission rules and PCAOB auditing standards; they are subject to a registrant's internal control over financial reporting (ICFR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjecting disclosures to audit and ICFR provides reasonable assurance, increases relevance and reliability, and mitigates concerns about consistency and quality. For accelerated filers (AFs) and large accelerated filers (LAFs), independent auditor must attest and report on management's assessment of ICFR. Inclusion increases compliance/audit costs but should streamline over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data requirement — Inline XBRL tagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related disclosures must be tagged in Inline XBRL on a phased-in basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging makes disclosures machine-readable, enabling aggregation, comparison, filtering, and enhanced analytics, reducing search costs and information-processing inefficiencies. Inline XBRL is expected to help analysts and retail investors via intermediaries. Filers already subject to Inline XBRL for other disclosures can leverage existing processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate taxonomy and limitations on custom tags
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will publish a climate taxonomy containing standard tags for each new disclosure; filers are prohibited from using custom tags unless there is no suitable standard tag in the taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A one-year transition period for tagging will allow taxonomy development and reduce need for custom tags. Inappropriate/excessive use of extensions (custom tags) would hinder benefits; prohibition and taxonomy aim to limit such use and improve data quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure thresholds for triggering financial statement note requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require disclosure if the aggregate amount of the absolute value of the effects of severe weather events or other natural conditions is less than one percent of pretax income for income statement effects or less than one percent of shareholders' equity for balance sheet effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De minimis absolute values (e.g., $100,000 and $500,000 referenced for certain companies) partially address concerns that the one percent threshold may be too low for some firms. Thresholds applied separately to income statement and balance sheet may produce partial disclosures (e.g., disclose income statement effects but not balance sheet effects). Some commenters objected to use of absolute values and to thresholds; thresholds simplify implementation and reduce burden but may omit decision-useful disclosures in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis thresholds and potential partial disclosure consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: De minimis values (illustrative examples: $100,000 and $500,000) may exceed one percent of denominators for some companies, and thresholds can result in partial disclosures or omission of decision-useful information depending on company-specific facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one threshold (income or balance sheet) is triggered, registrant need only disclose what the rule requires but may choose to disclose effects on both statements to avoid confusion. Commission acknowledges possibility of investors receiving a partial picture and allows registrants discretion to provide additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution principle — 'significant contributing factor'
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules use an attribution principle that requires registrants to disclose the entire capitalized cost, expenditure expensed, charge, or loss provided that a severe weather event or other natural condition was a 'significant contributing factor' to incurring the expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach mitigates commenter concerns about the complexity and cost of isolating or attributing portions of costs to climate events and avoids onerous tracking of line-item impacts. It may, however, create some litigation or classification risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to identify where amounts are presented in financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose where in the income statement or balance sheet the disclosed expenditures expensed, capitalized costs, charges, and losses are presented (i.e., line-item presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could result in incremental compliance costs but is mitigated because these amounts are captured in books and records and recognized under GAAP. Provides clarity for investors on presentation and facilitates extraction via Inline XBRL tagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to disclose beyond minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the rules set thresholds and specific disclosure requirements, nothing prevents a registrant from disclosing how a severe weather event or other natural condition affected both the income statement and balance sheet even if the disclosure threshold for one statement is not triggered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flexibility is intended to elicit disclosures that are both comparable and most relevant to investors without imposing unnecessary costs; registrants' discretion may lead to heterogeneity initially but comparability is expected to improve as best practices emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation — exclude broad 'transition activities' from financial statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce ambiguity, financial statement disclosures are limited to costs resulting from severe weather events and other natural conditions and to carbon offsets/RECs, rather than requiring disclosure of expenditures related to transition activities generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses hypotheticals (e.g., whether replacing a lightbulb with LED is a transition expense) and attribution questions (e.g., portion attributable to drought). The narrowed scope and revised attribution reduce ambiguity and comparability concerns compared with the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of recoveries related to severe weather events and natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose recoveries resulting from severe weather events and natural conditions if they are required to disclose capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, or losses incurred resulting from the same events or conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including recoveries allows investors to understand the net impact of severe weather events and natural conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified threshold calculation and removal of Financial Impact Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules removed the proposed Financial Impact Metrics (which would have required line-by-line financial impacts) and instead calculate the disclosure threshold once for impacts to the income statement and once for the balance sheet using as denominators income or loss before income tax expense or benefit and shareholders' equity or deficit, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifying thresholds reduces the number of calculations and allows registrants to estimate denominators earlier in the fiscal year, thereby reducing burdens compared to the proposal. Registrants may still need to track relevant expenditures throughout the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that comparability and data quality will improve over time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission expects comparability of disclosures to improve over time as registrants gain experience applying thresholds and attribution standards and as consensus emerges regarding best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial heterogeneity is acknowledged; audit, ICFR, taxonomy development, and practice convergence are expected to mitigate comparability issues and reduce costs over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs, burdens, and potential litigation/compliance risk considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of disclosures in financial statements and Inline XBRL increases compliance and audit costs, and differences in application could introduce incremental legal and compliance costs, including litigation risk stemming from classification of expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission expects these costs to be limited because the disclosed amounts are already recorded under GAAP, and anticipates costs to decrease as auditors and registrants gain experience. The Proposing Release and commenter surveys indicated wide heterogeneity in expected costs; registrants should account for internal/external costs, assurance fees, and potential system/control enhancements.
